topic: Peshwa rule and the Maratha confederacy II — mixed tiers
description: Bajirao I, Balaji Bajirao, Third Battle of Panipat (1761), Maratha confederacy, Anglo-Maratha wars

questions.stem: The first PESHWA of the Maratha empire who held the office as a hereditary office was:

options.option_text: Balaji Vishwanath Bhat (1713-1720)
Bajirao I, the celebrated military commander
Balaji Bajirao (also called Nanasaheb)
Madhavrao I, the youngest of the Peshwas

questions.explanation: Balaji Vishwanath — the FIRST hereditary Peshwa, appointed by Shahu Chhatrapati in 1713. Before him, the Peshwa office existed under Shivaji and his successors but was not hereditary. Balaji secured the Maratha 'sardeshmukhi' rights from the Mughals and laid the foundation of confederate Maratha rule. His son Bajirao I (1720-40) was the great expansionist. Grandson Balaji Bajirao / Nanasaheb (1740-61) expanded but lost at Panipat-3. Madhavrao I (1761-72) revived Maratha power after Panipat.

questions.stem: Bajirao I (Peshwa, 1720-40) is most remembered for:

options.option_text: Concluding peace with the Nizam of Hyderabad
Rapidly extending Maratha rule deep into north India
Capturing the Bahamani sultanate of Bijapur
Forming a permanent alliance with the British EIC

questions.explanation: Bajirao I — perhaps the greatest Maratha military commander; never lost a battle. Took Maratha cavalry as far as Delhi (1737), defeated the Nizam at Palkhed (1728) and Bhopal (1737-38). Rapidly extended Maratha rule beyond the Narmada into Malwa, Bundelkhand, Gujarat. Distractor 1 — Bajirao DEFEATED the Nizam, did not make peace. Distractor 3 — Bijapur was a Mughal province by then. Distractor 4 — anachronistic; the EIC was still consolidating coastal trade. Bajirao died young at 39 of fever in 1740.

questions.stem: The THIRD BATTLE OF PANIPAT (14 January 1761) was fought between:

options.option_text: Babur and the last Lodi sultan Ibrahim
The Marathas and Ahmad Shah Abdali of Afghanistan
Akbar's general Bairam Khan and Hemu
The British East India Company and Sirajuddaula

questions.explanation: Third Panipat (14 Jan 1761) — Marathas (commanded by Sadashivrao Bhau, with Vishwasrao the heir-apparent) vs Ahmad Shah Abdali / Durrani of Afghanistan (allied with Najib-ud-Daula and Shuja-ud-Daulah). Decisive Maratha defeat — ~50-70,000 Maratha casualties. Halted Maratha northward expansion at the worst possible moment for them. Distractor 1 = First Panipat (1526). Distractor 3 = Second Panipat (1556, Akbar vs Hemu). Distractor 4 = Battle of Plassey (1757).

questions.stem: After Panipat-3 (1761), Maratha power was revived under which young Peshwa?

options.option_text: Bajirao II (the last Peshwa, surrendered to British)
Madhavrao I (Peshwa 1761-72, revived the empire)
Narayanrao (Peshwa briefly, assassinated 1773)
Sawai Madhavrao (boy Peshwa under Nana Phadnavis)

questions.explanation: Madhavrao I — became Peshwa at age 16 in 1761, when the empire seemed broken after Panipat. In just 11 years he restored Maratha hegemony in the north (re-established suzerainty over Mughal emperor Shah Alam II in 1772), defeated the Nizam, suppressed Mysore raids. Died of TB at age 27 (1772). Often called the 'last great Peshwa'. After him decline set in. Distractor 1 — Bajirao II's tenure ended in surrender to the British in 1818. Distractor 3 — Narayanrao was murdered in 1773 by his uncle Raghunathrao's guards. Distractor 4 — Sawai Madhavrao reigned briefly as a child under Nana Phadnavis's regency.

questions.stem: The Maratha CONFEDERACY in the late 18th century included five major chiefs (sardars). Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

options.option_text: Holkar — Indore; Scindia — Gwalior; Bhonsle — Nagpur
Holkar — Pune; Gaekwad — Indore; Bhonsle — Mysore
Scindia — Pune; Holkar — Tanjore; Gaekwad — Lucknow
Bhonsle — Bijapur; Scindia — Mysore; Holkar — Cuttack

questions.explanation: Maratha confederacy seats (after consolidation): PESHWA — Pune (titular head). HOLKAR — Indore. SCINDIA / SHINDE — Gwalior (and Ujjain). BHONSLE — Nagpur (a different branch from Shivaji's family who ruled in Maharashtra and Tanjore). GAEKWAD — Baroda (Vadodara, Gujarat). Each chief was largely autonomous; only loosely answered to the Peshwa. This decentralisation was a strategic strength but a coordination weakness in the Anglo-Maratha wars.

questions.stem: The Treaty of Bassein (December 1802), which placed the Peshwa under British 'subsidiary alliance', triggered the:

options.option_text: First Anglo-Maratha War (Salbai treaty, 1782)
Second Anglo-Maratha War (1803-05, Wellesley)
Third Anglo-Maratha War (1817-18, Hastings)
First Anglo-Sikh War (1845-46, Hardinge)

questions.explanation: Treaty of Bassein (Dec 1802) — Bajirao II, after losing to Holkar, fled to British protection and signed this treaty accepting subsidiary alliance and a British force at Pune. The other Maratha sardars (Scindia, Bhonsle, Holkar) saw this as betrayal and the Second Anglo-Maratha War (1803-05) followed under Lord Wellesley → Battles of Assaye (Arthur Wellesley, future Duke of Wellington), Argaon, Laswari. Treaty of Salbai (1782) ended the First war. Third war (1817-18) under Lord Hastings ended the Maratha confederacy entirely.

questions.stem: The LAST Peshwa, who was defeated by the British in 1818 and exiled to Bithur near Kanpur, was:

options.option_text: Madhavrao Narayan, the boy Peshwa of Pune
Bajirao II, son of Raghunathrao 'Raghoba'
Balaji Bajirao, defeated earlier at Panipat
Bajirao I, the great expansionist of the north

questions.explanation: Bajirao II — the last Peshwa. Surrendered after the Third Anglo-Maratha War (June 1818, Battle of Koregaon-Bhima earlier in Jan 1818). Accepted a pension of ₹8 lakh/year and was exiled to Bithur (near Kanpur). His adopted son was NANA SAHIB — leader of the 1857 revolt at Kanpur. Distractor 1 — Madhavrao Narayan died young in 1795. Distractor 3 — Balaji Bajirao (Nanasaheb) died of grief shortly after Panipat-3. Distractor 4 — Bajirao I died in 1740.
